# Emissary Docs

> Emissary is a platform for LLM model routing, post-training and inference. Route each request to the model best suited to handle it, post-train models of your own, and serve base and fine-tuned models on managed GPU infrastructure.

Emissary's model router is reached through one gateway URL that is compatible with the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs. Pages are plain prose with short answers first. A single-file version of every page below is at https://docs.withemissary.com/llms-full.txt.

## Overview

- [Emissary docs: LLM routing, post-training, inference](https://docs.withemissary.com): Emissary is a platform for LLM model routing, post-training and inference. Route requests to the right model, train your own, and serve it on managed GPUs.
- [LLM routing, post-training and inference glossary](https://docs.withemissary.com/glossary): Definitions of the terms used across the Emissary docs: model router, gateway, confidence threshold, effort, SFT, GRPO, LoRA, checkpoint, engine and more.

## Quickstarts

- [ModelRouter quickstart: your first LLM router](https://docs.withemissary.com/quickstart/router): Create a router that sends each query to the best-suited model in about 56 ms for $0.23 per 10k requests. Use the public playground, the dashboard or the API.
- [LLM-as-a-judge quickstart: create your first judge](https://docs.withemissary.com/quickstart/llm-as-judge): Create an LLM judge that scores any text against criteria you define and returns a calibrated probability in about 56 ms. Use the playground, dashboard or API.
- [Experiments: zero-shot LLM deployments in minutes](https://docs.withemissary.com/experiment): Spin up a zero-shot model in under a minute and call it through a ready-made API: judge, decision, routing, tool calling, regression and NER modes.

## Model routing

- [What is model routing? LLM routers explained](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/what-is-model-routing): Model routing sends each LLM request to the model best suited to handle it. Learn how an LLM router works, the types of routers, and when to use one.
- [Why use model routing? Benefits and trade-offs](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/why-route): Why route across LLMs instead of picking one model: better performance, typically 30-50% lower cost, lower latency, easier migration, and when not to route.
- [How to reduce LLM costs with model routing](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/reduce-llm-costs): Cut LLM API spend by routing each request to the cheapest model that can do the job. Where the savings come from, typical results, and how to measure them.
- [Get started: create your first LLM router](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/get-started): Create an Emissary router in the dashboard, send a request through the OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible gateway, and see how it was routed. About ten minutes.
- [How an LLM router decides which model to use](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/how-routing-works/decision): How Emissary decides which LLM serves a request: estimate each model's confidence, keep the confident ones, then pick the cheapest. Includes a worked example.
- [What an LLM router sees: cache, effort and cost](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/how-routing-works/what-the-router-sees): The signals Emissary's router uses beyond the request: prompt cache state, expected output length, reasoning effort, modality, context limits and your pricing.
- [Types of LLM routers: the router design space](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/how-routing-works/design-space): How LLM routers differ: complexity-based vs performance-based, blind vs model-aware, stateless vs stateful. A neutral map for evaluating any router.
- [LLM router vs LLM gateway: the difference](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/how-routing-works/routers-and-gateways): A router decides which model serves a request, and a gateway handles how requests reach models. See the difference and how Emissary can be both.
- [Choose models for your LLM router catalog](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/guides/choose-your-models): Build your router's model catalog and pick a default model, with three starting points: open-source only, closed-source only, and a mixed catalog.
- [Confidence threshold: quality vs cost in routing](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/guides/confidence-threshold): The confidence threshold is the main quality-versus-cost dial on a router: how sure it must be that a model can handle a request. Learn how to tune it.
- [Use your own LLM pricing in a router](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/guides/pricing): Router pricing is prefilled with list prices. Adjust it to your contract rates so the router's idea of cheapest is your cheapest.
- [Migrate to new LLMs with model routing](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/guides/migrate-to-new-models): Adopt new LLMs without guesswork: the router scores models you haven't enabled, so you can see when one could take a meaningful share of your traffic.
- [Connect an app or agent to an LLM router](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/guides/connect): Call an Emissary router from the OpenAI or Anthropic SDK, curl or plain HTTP, or point a coding agent such as Claude Code at the gateway.
- [Monitor and debug LLM routing decisions](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/guides/monitor-and-debug): Use the Activity, Metrics, Sessions and Configuration tabs to see how a router behaves, read a routing decision in detail, and diagnose unexpected routing.
- [What emerges from LLM routing](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/insights): Routing records each model's confidence on every request, giving you workload insight and a path to dedicated inference and post-training on your own traffic.
- [Model routing FAQ: LLM router questions](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/faq): Short answers to common questions about LLM model routing: routers versus gateways, quality, cost, latency, supported models and when not to route.

## Comparing and evaluating LLM routers

- [LLM router comparison: OpenRouter, LiteLLM and more](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/evaluate/llm-router-comparison): Compare LLM routers and gateways: Emissary, OpenRouter, LiteLLM, Not Diamond and Router.com. How each chooses a model and where each fits best.
- [Emissary vs OpenRouter: model vs provider routing](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/evaluate/emissary-vs-openrouter): Emissary vs OpenRouter: a trained, capability-aware router and gateway versus a unified marketplace API with provider routing and an auto-router.
- [Emissary vs LiteLLM: router vs gateway](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/evaluate/emissary-vs-litellm): Emissary vs LiteLLM: automated, trained model routing with tracked savings versus a self-hosted gateway with broad model coverage and self-managed rules.
- [Emissary vs Not Diamond: routing compared](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/evaluate/emissary-vs-notdiamond): Emissary vs Not Diamond: per-request, per-model success prediction versus Not Diamond Code's routing from metadata such as a complexity classification.
- [Emissary vs Router.com: routing compared](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/evaluate/emissary-vs-router-com): Emissary vs Router.com (Ramp): an automated, capability-aware router versus a gateway with pluggable routing policies and finance integration.
- [How to test an LLM router on your traffic](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/evaluate/run-a-trial): Test a router on your own requests before moving production traffic: build a sample, set a baseline, compare cost, latency and quality, and read the decisions.
- [LLM router selection checklist](https://docs.withemissary.com/routing/evaluate/selection-checklist): A checklist for evaluating model routers: fit, decision quality, state and cost, modality, integration and evidence. Use it on any router, including Emissary.

## Post-training

- [What is post-training? SFT, GRPO and fine-tuning](https://docs.withemissary.com/fine-tuning/what-is-post-training): Post-training adapts a base LLM to your task by changing its weights. Learn how SFT and GRPO work, what you need, and how to start post-training on Emissary.
- [Post-training quickstart: fine-tune a model](https://docs.withemissary.com/fine-tuning/quickstart): Fine-tune your first model on Emissary: create a project, upload a dataset, run a training job, compare checkpoints, and deploy the best one.
- [Post-training concepts: SFT, GRPO, checkpoints](https://docs.withemissary.com/fine-tuning/concept): Core concepts behind post-training on Emissary: projects, datasets, base models, SFT and GRPO, training jobs, checkpoints, evaluation and deployment.
- [Post-training datasets: formats and schemas](https://docs.withemissary.com/fine-tuning/datasets): How to format and upload datasets for post-training on Emissary: supported formats, per-task schemas, profiling and best practices.
- [Post-training hyperparameters for SFT and GRPO](https://docs.withemissary.com/fine-tuning/parameters): The hyperparameters you can tune when post-training on Emissary with SFT and GRPO, what each one does, and how to adjust them.

## Inference

- [What is LLM inference? Engines and autoscaling](https://docs.withemissary.com/inference/what-is-llm-inference): LLM inference is running a trained model to produce outputs. See how Emissary serves base and fine-tuned models on managed GPUs with autoscaling.
- [Inference concepts: engines and deployments](https://docs.withemissary.com/inference/concept): Inference engines, deployments, server types, autoscaling and lifecycle on Emissary: how base and fine-tuned models are served on managed GPUs.
- [Deployments: serve base and fine-tuned models](https://docs.withemissary.com/inference/deployments): How deployments serve base and fine-tuned LoRA models on an Emissary inference engine: creating, calling and managing them.
- [Autoscaling LLM inference: replicas and tuning](https://docs.withemissary.com/inference/autoscaling): How Emissary cluster engines scale GPU replicas up and down with traffic: min and max replicas, scaling metrics, delays and tuning.

## API reference

- [Emissary API reference](https://docs.withemissary.com/api): REST endpoints for projects, datasets, training jobs, inference engines and deployments.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Emissary-Tech/emissary-api-docs/refs/heads/main/api/openapi.yaml): machine-readable API definition.
